purpose: Recover the real TYFZA1 OMCI MIB plugins and follow capability population instead of relying on empty partial-extraction placeholders or plugin defaults.
findings: The original ubi_r0 volume has a .ubifs filename but contains SquashFS. unsquashfs -cat recovered only the named ELF files, without extracting the full filesystem. The freshly extracted libomci_mib.so hash matches the original selected sample.

MIB_Table_Init symbol ambiguity was resolved at exact entry0x10e3c8. The loader discovers /lib/omci plugins and calls their mibTable_init functions; recovered plugins provide the actual ONU2-G, T-CONT, priority queue and scheduler definitions.

omci_app FUN_0040e2fc initializes MIB defaults and then fills ONU2-G queue/scheduler/GEM counts from gInfo fields at0x442ab8/0x442ab0/0x442ab4. omci_mib_cfg_setup_me performs the same overrides for configured MEs.

OMCI_Init reads device capabilities through omci_wrapper_getDevCapabilities into gInfo+0x98 before MIB construction. Plugin default capability constants therefore do not establish the actual values advertised to an OLT.
TcontDrvCfg distinguishes XGTC14-bit Alloc-ID range from GPON12-bit range; recovered code does not justify narrowing the native XGTC range.
open_questions: Complete the driver capability transport/structure interpretation and runtime input values before comparing final counts with the native31 business T-CONTs,280 priority queues and248 GEM capacity.
The available static data does not establish whether a capacity discrepancy exists on the peer OLT path; no speculative capacity reduction or QoS flag copy was made.
analysis_limits: One attempted decompile address0x14cfd8 was not a mapped code location; its explicit tool error is preserved. The valid exact entry and MIB plugin analyses succeeded.
These are shipped binary analyses and extraction checks, not a running stock OMCI MIB capture.
No production source change or hardware correctness claim follows solely from these recovered defaults.
